tests.name: A payment over the spend limit waits for password confirmation
tests.summary:
Requested a $150 rent payment to @ada.
Entered “pay @ada 150 for rent” and selected the $150.00 payment option.
Reviewed the confirmation showing $150.00 to @ada and the per-payment limit, then entered the provided password and confirmed the payment.
The payment was completed, and the page confirmed: “Sent $150.00 to @ada.”

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
Checked the link https://phantorn-airdrop.app/claim using the Quick check option.
The result marked the link as Dangerous.
The reasons stated that the address imitates Phantom.

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
The automated run moved through the page without preserving a verifiable view of the scan-result details. It recognized “Dangerous” twice, but did not successfully anchor the accompanying reason text before making the final assertion.
Update the automation to wait for the result panel, target the reason text within that panel, and verify it is visible before asserting. Avoid broad scrolling or navigation-prone targets after submitting the scan.

tests.name: Shield refuses to save a look-alike of a saved person
tests.summary:
Entered the name “Ada new” and the provided wallet address on the People page.
Selected “Save person.”
The page reported that the address was not saved because it looks like Ada’s saved address but is not.
“Ada new” was not added to the people list.

tests.name: Paying a name that is both a saved person and another user asks who you meant
tests.summary:
Requested a $5 payment to Semi for coffee.
Entered “pay semi 5 for coffee” and selected the Pay $5.00 button.
The page asked which Semi was intended and showed both “Your contact Semi” and “Mlyfo user @semi”.
Selected “Your contact Semi”, and the page confirmed: “Sent $5.00 to Semi.”

tests.name: The Android keyboard hands a copied address to Shield
tests.summary:
The test was configured to open the /k address after sign-in, but that address returned a 404 page instead of the Shield page.
Update the test to use the actual Shield route (for example, navigate through the Shield menu) and verify that its address query is supported.

tests.name: The Android keyboard hands a copied address to Shield
tests.summary:
The test was given the /k address, but that address returned a Not Found page instead of the expected Shield page.
Update the scenario with the deployed Shield page address, or deploy and verify the /k route before rerunning.

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved Ethereum and Base address
tests.summary:
The address check sent a valid-looking 0x address through Solana validation, so it never compared it with Ada (Base)'s saved address or showed the expected Ethereum and Base result.
Update Shield's address detection so 0x addresses are handled as Ethereum and Base addresses before any Solana validation, then run the saved-contact look-alike comparison.
evidence: error_ui_text: Blocked. This isn’t a valid Solana address.
evidence: objective_contradiction: POST https://mlyfo.vercel.app/api/shield/address -> 200

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved Ethereum and Base address
tests.summary:
The address checker is using the wrong network rules for the entered address, so it does not recognize the Ethereum/Base address or match it to Ada (Base)'s saved address.
Update Shield’s address detection so 0x-prefixed Ethereum/Base addresses are evaluated as EVM addresses and can trigger the saved-contact look-alike warning.
evidence: error_ui_text: Blocked. This isn’t a valid Solana address.
